display.title: Erev Chof Av: Reb Levi Yitzchak and the Secret Chuppah
display.summary_short: For the Rebbe's father's yahrzeit, how Reb Levi Yitzchak made a secret Jewish wedding under Soviet watch, and how two informers became devoted Chassidim.
display.summary_long: On the eve of Chof Av, the yahrzeit of the Rebbe's father, the storyteller tells of Reb Levi Yitzchak, the Rav of Yekaterinoslav, who taught Torah with mesiras nefesh while the Soviet police closed shuls and arrested rabbis. A Jewish superintendent downstairs recorded every visitor for the police. Late one night a woman begs him to marry her daughter and her groom, both government workers, in secret. Reb Levi Yitzchak wakes neighbors one by one to make a minyan, skipping a man he suspects of informing, but is still one short, so he knocks on the superintendent's door. The wedding takes place, and afterwards two men stay behind, the superintendent and the man he had trusted, hand over their Communist Party cards and ask to become Chassidim. The storyteller compares the police to the yetzer hara that tries to stop our mitzvos, asks for extra tzedakah and the pesukim in honor of the day, and leads the children in a niggun of Reb Levi Yitzchak, Yehi Ratzon and a song wishing everyone a ksivah vachasimah tovah.
display.lesson: Stand up to the yetzer hara the way Reb Levi Yitzchak stood up to the Soviet police, and never give up on any Jew.
